rows.acceptance: Pin C# Studio backend, Studio JS/CSS and Rust engine/desktop commit SHAs in a machine-readable baseline; all parity claims name those SHAs.

rows.acceptance: Every visible web feature, route-derived behavior and desktop-only behavior has owner, source path, status, test and waiver; omissions fail the audit.

rows.requirement: Distinguish behavioral parity from implementation parity
rows.acceptance: REST and browser storage are replaced by in-process native mechanisms; parity tests compare behavior, not transport or widget technology.
rows.scope_note: Transport-to-native mapping plus the consequences for parity tests.

rows.acceptance: Desktop commands use the same Rust kernel as Rust runner; no math/parser/precision semantics are reimplemented in widgets or renderer.
rows.scope_note: RealEngine owns lovelace_lang::Engine and delegates eval/format; no math semantics in the desktop.

rows.acceptance: Release remains blocked when any P0 acceptance test is absent, skipped, stale, unrun or failed, regardless of headless suite count.

rows.acceptance: Every non-parity choice has human-approved rationale, expiry/review criterion and evidence; absence is not counted as equivalence.
rows.scope_note: Seven deviations with owner, status, rationale, review criterion and evidence.

rows.acceptance: Record deterministic reference state/output/diagnostics/plots for the named web Studio journeys and execute corresponding desktop scenarios.

rows.requirement: Separate visual, functional and performance acceptance
rows.acceptance: Release scorecard reports three independent gates and never substitutes screenshots for semantics or engine unit tests for real-window behavior.
Publish Windows, Linux and macOS target matrix, clearly marking initial release and later ports; no platform claim without a built, run GUI test.

rows.acceptance: Delivery plan prioritizes editor responsiveness, real cancellation, readability, working plots and useful inspection before optional decoration.

rows.requirement: Choose and validate a native rendering stack
rows.acceptance: Run a time-boxed spike comparing candidate Rust UI frameworks against real editor, accessibility, text/IME, plotting and docking acceptance scenarios; record choice.

rows.acceptance: Production desktop has no embedded webview, JavaScript engine or mandatory localhost service; application operates with all network interfaces disabled.

rows.acceptance: Headless app state and commands are independent of platform window handles; native renderer consumes state and publishes typed commands.
Worker emits RunStarted/StepStarted/StepComputed/StepReused/SubProgress/Output/Plot/Diagnostic/Completed/Cancelled with run and document IDs.

rows.requirement: Never execute evaluation on the UI thread
rows.acceptance: Even a 30-second script leaves pointer, keyboard, window close, pane resize and animations responsive; automated GUI watchdog verifies.
Only one computation mutates a document engine at a time; concurrent requests are rejected or queued with clear UI policy.

rows.requirement: Permit independent documents to run concurrently
rows.acceptance: With tab A busy, tab B can run and cancel and tab A continues unaffected; no process-wide engine lock.
Every event has document ID, run ID, source revision and sequence; events from obsolete revisions never overwrite current pane state.
Worker passes a cooperative token into evaluator, high-precision math and symbolic loops; cancellation interrupts a test operation rather than only setting UI state.
rows.scope_note: Live Arc<AtomicBool> in lovelace_symbolics::cancel, armed per evaluation; single matmul kernel cancelled in 19.72 ms (gui-selftest) / 126 ms (desktop t9). Evidence class corrected from gui to unit (DEC-008): the requirement is a mechanism, not a window behaviour.

rows.acceptance: UI gets typed numeric, array, record, symbolic and diagnostic projections; display text is not reparsed to infer structure.
Platform-specific unsafe code stays in small adapters with reviewed invariants; shared UI, workspace, execution and settings logic is safe Rust.

rows.requirement: Resist unbounded memory and event queues
rows.acceptance: Progress and output delivery has coalescing/backpressure and bounded storage without losing terminal events, final result or required diagnostics.
Product design describes a calm scientific workbench: information-dense, precise, low-noise, professional; final screens are reviewed against reference mockups.

rows.requirement: Ship excellent dark and light themes

UI uses legible proportional controls and configurable monospaced code/output; titles, labels, table text and metadata have consistent hierarchy.
No gradients, heavy glass effects or gratuitous animations obscure content; active pane, selection, errors and actions remain legible in both themes.
Every button/input/tab/menu/popup/splitter implements rest, hover, pressed, disabled, selected, focus and error states with consistent interaction.

rows.requirement: Provide semantic color without color dependence

First launch and empty variables/functions/plots/logs/inspector panes explain what to do next and offer an appropriate next action.
Normal text reaches WCAG AA 4.5:1 and large text/non-text UI indicators reach 3:1 in each theme, validated from rendered colors.

rows.acceptance: One consistent icon family, stroke weight and size; icons with ambiguous meaning include visible text or tooltips with shortcut.

rows.requirement: Allow plot history within a session
rows.acceptance: Optional mini-gallery allows compare/return to previous plots with source and timestamp; feature cannot gate web parity.
Repeated polls/events, reruns and cancellation never duplicate print lines or change order; byte-sensitive tests cover line endings.
rows.scope_note: Byte-exact CRLF/LF/CR preserved (61 0D 0A 62 63 0A 64 65 0D 66); replay watermark stops duplicate log lines; cancel and rerun keep each line exactly once; 174 tests pass.

rows.acceptance: Logs distinguish echo, stdout, result, diagnostic, timing and progress with readable icons, text and timestamps optional.
rows.scope_note: All seven kinds now have real producers: echo (quick eval), stdout, result, diagnostic, timing, progress, info; markers and order visible across the two captures.

rows.acceptance: Enter executes active session command and clears input only after accepting request; previous commands are navigable with keyboard.
rows.scope_note: Input clears only after acceptance; busy refusal keeps text and logs an advisory; previous commands navigable newest-first; echo emitted exactly once per submission.

rows.acceptance: Click diagnostic opens and focuses source, highlights position, and provides copyable full error details.
Copy selected, copy all, clear current view and save log actions work with keyboard and context menu.
When storage cap is reached show truncated-history indicator and offer export of available full run log if configured; never hide current fatal error.
Display total and per-statement elapsed with units; cached runs identify reused count and avoid implying reused output was recomputed.
Filter by errors, outputs, run and document without changing stored event order.
Success/fail/cancel indication visible without intrusive modal; long-running jobs receive optional desktop notification only by user opt-in.

rows.requirement: Keep performance stable under log load
rows.acceptance: A run with 100k log records remains scrollable via virtualization and bounded live updates; no quadratic text-control replacement.
All commands and pane actions accessible without mouse; an automated keyboard journey completes primary tasks.

rows.requirement: Support screen reader roles and names
rows.acceptance: Windows UIA and corresponding platform accessibility trees expose name/role/value/state for editor, tabs, tables, buttons and progress.
Every focusable control has visible 3:1 focus indicator; focus never becomes invisible in dark or light mode.
125â€“200% DPI/text scale retains readable buttons/labels and usable layout without clipped content.
Users can configure mono font and 12â€“24 pt range, line-height and optionally ligatures; all decorations remain aligned.
OS theme change updates controls and plot chrome without losing user focus, run or document state.
Help > Keyboard Shortcuts and command palette display all global and editor shortcuts.

rows.requirement: Avoid conflicts with IME and screen readers
rows.acceptance: Text composition and shortcut accelerators do not steal native IME shortcuts or screen-reader navigation.
High contrast appearance uses semantic tokens rather than merely raising window brightness; contrast validated.
OS reduced-motion preference disables decorative animations while retaining progress values and completion feedback.
Most interactive targets are >=32Ã—32 logical pixels; compact density exceptions preserve alternative keyboard access.
Errors include icon, text and location; color-blind tests identify errors and successes without hue.
Controls and errors use concise, predictable text; abbreviations have tooltips; accessible description includes action and consequence.
ASCII/Unicode setting updates structured result, workspace and logs consistently; missing glyphs fall back without tofu squares.

rows.requirement: Support native file dialogs and clipboard
rows.acceptance: Open/Save/Save As, paste and clipboard integration work via OS APIs with expected keyboard shortcuts.
App launches, evaluates, plots and opens files with network disabled; no HTTP listener or surprise external requests.
Embedded SVG external references and active content do not trigger network/file reads or script execution.
Saving to existing changed file prompts before overwrite; atomic temp-write/rename and recovery preserve original on failure.
Fonts fall back to OS-installed fonts; syntax/theme/icon assets are bundled or resolved offline; no CDN at runtime.
Windows APPDATA, Linux XDG, macOS Application Support are used; no writes to installed binary directory by default.
rows.scope_note: App-scoped %APPDATA%\\Lovelace\\plots is resolved and the refusal is explicit; runtime write is denied to child processes in this session (EVD-058), so no successful APPDATA write can be shown here.

rows.acceptance: Signed or notarized where applicable, versioned binaries for supported OS/arch, reliable uninstall and OS integration.
Opening a .ls file from shell launches or focuses desktop with that file, without unexpected execution.

rows.requirement: Expose clear error on unsupported platform
rows.acceptance: A platform without UI support is explicitly marked unsupported by release metadata, not silently shipped as headless placeholder.
Keyboard modifiers, dialogs, caret/IME, clipboard and DPI tested on every advertised platform.
User can export redacted app version/config/logs for bug reports without private source content unless explicitly opted in.
On reference machine cold start to interactive editor p95 <= 2.0 s and warm start <= 1.0 s; measure signed release binary.
Typing/caret movement p95 <= 16 ms and no input freeze >100 ms under normal work, measured with a live GUI profiler.
500 KB/5k-line document maintains >=55 fps p95 scrolling on reference desktop; 10k-line stress run is explicitly reported.
Run button/shortcut acknowledges within 100 ms; worker scheduling not blocked by rendering or queued logs.
rows.scope_note: Run acknowledgement 72 ms measured, bound 100 ms; submit 96 microseconds and worker scheduling not blocked by render (engine_build_enter on worker at +393 microseconds).

rows.acceptance: Cancel action updates visible state within 100 ms and invokes token immediately; termination meets RUN cancellation bound for cooperative workloads.
rows.scope_note: Esc -> run Cancelled in 48.3 ms (this run), 70.8 and 72.5 ms earlier; bound 100 ms for visible acknowledgement, 2 s for termination.

rows.acceptance: Updating 10k variable/function rows takes <=200 ms to visible state via diff/virtualization, without recreating all children.
Typical SVG <100 KB fits pane in <=250 ms after receipt; complex >1 MB remains interactive and shows pending state.
Idle process does not continuously poll at high rate or consume >2% of one reference CPU core; measure with window open.

rows.requirement: Avoid quadratic undo and text copying
rows.acceptance: 10k typed characters do not cause unbounded full-buffer clones per keystroke; memory/CPU profiling confirms acceptable scaling.
Invalid config and recovery files produce warning/default/backup, never launch crash or unrecoverable data loss.

rows.requirement: Monitor resource budgets for enormous math
rows.acceptance: Extreme precision requests receive estimated memory/time warning or budget refusal; no uncontrolled process abort for documented refusal classes.
Renderer crash or invalid plot does not corrupt engine/document; recoverable error surfaces and next run still works.

rows.requirement: Maintain a golden web-to-desktop journey suite
rows.acceptance: Each reference journey has input, action sequence, expected state/events/plots, desktop driver and a reproducible result artifact.

rows.requirement: Run actual native GUI end-to-end tests
rows.acceptance: CI or dedicated test VM launches a window and drives pointer/keyboard; headless AppState selftest alone cannot satisfy GUI gate.
Baseline screenshots at 900Ã—600, 1280Ã—800, 1920Ã—1080 and 100/150/200% scale reviewed for both themes.

rows.requirement: Test real cancellation with a slow kernel
rows.acceptance: GUI test cancels a script while worker is inside lengthy computation; asserts UI responsiveness, state consistency and worker termination.
Two tabs execute with different precision and variables concurrently; snapshots and plots never cross, and tab B completes while A runs.
Random edit sequences compare incremental run snapshot to fresh-run reference across dependencies, functions, effects and precision.

rows.requirement: Test editor and diagnostic UTF-16 mapping
rows.acceptance: Emoji, combining marks, CRLF, multiline, nested scopes and parse errors highlight exact location with correct accessible announcement.
Golden outputs cover exact fractions, 1k-digit numbers, matrix/inverse, solve records, MathIR, symbols, conditions and truncated prints.
Reference plot corpus rasterized in both renderers; text, strokes and clip regions compared with documented pixel tolerance and manual review.
Crash during dirty buffer edit and interrupted save are replayed; user data remains recoverable and app relaunches cleanly.

rows.requirement: Test screen reader and keyboard flows
rows.acceptance: One Windows UIA screen reader and one other supported platform accessibility path are exercised; all primary actions reachable.
At least 5 target users complete 8 scripted tasks; >=90% task success, median <2 min for common tasks, and document qualitative friction.
rows.scope_note: Human usability sessions (>=5 target users) cannot be produced by this run; waived by the user in DEC-006. Never reported as PASS.

rows.acceptance: Target System Usability Scale >=80 in pilot, with no unresolved severity-1 usability finding at launch.

rows.requirement: Audit layout/content across DPI and text scaling
rows.acceptance: Visual tests at 100/125/150/200% DPI plus system text enlargement identify no overlapping/clipped primary controls.
Theme token checker verifies normal text >=4.5:1 and large/control indicators >=3:1; exemptions documented.
Artifact manifest records OS, build SHA, Rust toolchain, source hash, GUI test results, screenshot bundle and test fixture checksums.

rows.requirement: Make unsupported features visible, not silently skipped
rows.acceptance: Feature register distinguishes PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, NOT_TESTED, APPROVED_DEVIATION; missing evidence blocks final parity.
Continuous measurements compare startup/input/frame metrics and task completion across releases, with declared regression thresholds.
